prerequisites: Basic knowledge in innovation, management, business administration, finance, human resource management and leadership.

learning_outcomes.text: Describe the theoretical foundation and core concepts of technology-based entrepreneurship.
Analyze technological trends and identify entrepreneurial opportunities.
Evaluate the role of intellectual property as a competitive advantage for a technology-based start-up.
Apply the disciplined entrepreneurship approach to systematically develop a business idea.
Critically discuss the differences between the concepts of discovery and creation in entrepreneurship.
Develop the integration of technical product development and market-oriented business model development into coherent venture strategies.
Develop and refine ideas based on feedback, and organize teamwork in groups.
Professionally give and receive constructive feedback.
Plan and execute tasks in projects with advice from practitioners.

syllabus_topics: The 'why' and 'what' questions of technology management
Fundamental theories and concepts (discovery vs. creation)
Empirical evidence for start-up practice and success
Technological development and strategic technology management (IP, ecosystems, financing, etc.)
From initial idea to validated market offering
